newsitem.title: USA: US 21ST CENTURY FARM POLICY PANEL TAKING SHAPE.
newsitem.headline: US 21ST CENTURY FARM POLICY PANEL TAKING SHAPE.

text.p: A blue-ribbon panel charged with recommending policies to lead U.S. agriculture into the next century is beginning to take shape.

On Thursday, Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar, an Indianna Republican, announced his four selections for the Commission on 21st Century Production Agriculture, which was authorized by the 1996 farm bill.
Last year, after winning election to the Senate, then-House Agriculture Committee Chairman Pat Roberts, a Kansas Republican, announced his four selections.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman will fill out the 11-member panel with three of his own choices.
In a statement, Lugar noted there now enough members for the panel to begin meeting.

The commission's first task is to issue a report by June 1, 1998 on the effectiveness of reforms made in 1996 farm act. That legislation eliminated most government planting restrictions previously tied to crop subsidy payments.

It will also look at the U.S. food security situation in respect to trade, international competitiveness, consumer prices and crop supplies. Other areas for review include the tax and regulatory burden on farmers and the effect that 1996 farm act has had on farm land values.

The commission will make a second report by January 1, 2001 outlining its recommendations for future role of the government in agriculture. Current farm programs expire in 2002 and a new round of international trade talks begin in 2000.
The four members appointed by Lugar are:
--Don Villock, an Indiana grain farmer who served as executive director of that state's USDA Agricultural Stabilization and Conservation Service office during the Bush Administration.
--Bruce Brumfied, a Mississippi cotton, grain and catfish farmer and former president and chairman of the National Cotton Council of America.
--Charles Kruse, a grain and cotton farmer who is currently president of the Missouri Farm Bureau. Kruse is also a former director of the Missouri Department of Agriculture.
--William Northey, an Iowa farmer and former president of the National Corn Growers Association.
